text.p: The FTSE 100 index will give a restrained performance on Thursday, trying to edge up towards 4,885. But lack of buying interest may then send it floating back to around 4,860, technical analysts said.
The FTSE showed little desire to stay above 4,900 on Wednesday despite record highs achieved by the main European bourses as well as by Wall Street and so it may begin to flatten out, they added.
Shares in the financial sector are expected to add a little to Wednesday's gains but utilities may also push ahead.
By 0726 GMT, the FTSE was indicated down 0.1 to 4,874.4.
On Wednesday, France's CAC 40 index made a new high for the year closing up 82.4 points to 3,003.53 and Germany's DAX index shot up 175.67 to 4,406.09.
"But the FTSE fell back below 4,900 (yesterday) and does not look like it's going to go too far away from its overnight close (at 4,874.5)," said one analyst.

The index achieved a near two-thirds retracement of the 200 point fall to its intra-day low of 4,794.9 on July 21 from a high of 4,998.1 on July 18. But with the advance/decline ratio for the FTSE only a little over two-to-one yesterday, the market will now have a tendency to pause in an uptrend, analysts said.
